title: Wi-Fi temperature logger
desc: Read temperature and humidity and show them on a small web page served by the board itself.

title: Line-following robot
needs: Arduino, 2 motors, motor driver, IR sensors
desc: A two-wheeled car that follows black tape. A classic first robot that teaches sensors and control loops.

title: Plant watering reminder
desc: Light an LED or send a message when the soil gets dry. Capacitive sensors last longer than the bare-metal resistive kind.

title: Pan-tilt camera mount
needs: 2 hobby servos, joystick or web page
desc: Drive two servos to aim a camera. Power the servos from their own supply, not from a pin on the board.

title: Obstacle-avoiding rover
needs: Chassis kit, ultrasonic sensor, motor driver
desc: Drive forward, measure distance, and turn away from walls. Then add smoother behaviour with a simple state machine.

title: Traffic lights
desc: Run a pedestrian crossing sequence without using delay(), so that the button always responds.

title: Reaction timer
desc: Light an LED after a random wait and measure how fast you hit the button. Keep a high score.

title: Parking sensor
desc: Beep faster as an object gets closer, like the sensor in a car bumper.

title: Desktop radar
desc: Sweep the sensor on a servo and draw what it sees as a radar screen on your computer.

title: Light-seeking robot
desc: Build a Braitenberg vehicle, then swap the two wires and watch it flee the light.

title: E-paper weather display
desc: Show the forecast on a screen that keeps its picture with the power off.

title: Desk air monitor
desc: Measure CO2 at your desk and light up when it is time to open a window.

title: LED matrix clock
desc: A clock that sets itself over Wi-Fi and scrolls the date now and then.

title: Cardboard robot arm
desc: A small arm controlled by turning knobs. Record a sequence of moves and replay it.

title: Morse code key
desc: Tap out Morse code and have the board decode it to text on the serial monitor.

title: Light theremin
desc: Wave a hand over a light sensor to change the pitch. Noisy and very satisfying.

title: Motion night light
desc: A strip that fades up when someone walks past in the dark and fades out again.

title: Self-balancing robot
desc: Two wheels and a PID loop. Expect to spend most of the time tuning three numbers.

title: Doorbell notifier
desc: Detect the doorbell and send a message to your phone over your home network.

title: Web-controlled rover
desc: Drive a small rover from a web page served by the robot itself.
